recent_events.title: Marie-Philippe Bouchard takes office as new CBC/Radio-Canada President and CEO
recent_events.description: Marie-Philippe Bouchard began her five-year term as President and CEO, succeeding Catherine Tait. She is the first Francophone woman to lead the corporation. Her appointment comes at a critical time with funding challenges and political pressure from Conservative threats to defund the CBC.
recent_events.impact: Leadership transition during a period of existential challenges for the public broadcaster, including digital transformation and political uncertainty

recent_events.title: 2025 federal election: CBC funding becomes a major campaign issue
recent_events.description: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre campaigned on defunding the CBC entirely, while Liberal Leader Mark Carney promised an initial $150 million increase in annual CBC funding. The election highlighted the polarized political debate over public broadcasting in Canada.
recent_events.impact: CBC funding emerged as a defining wedge issue in Canadian federal politics, with the Liberal victory ensuring continued public broadcaster support

recent_events.title: CBC/Radio-Canada launches 2025-2030 corporate strategy 'CBC, Here for Canada'
recent_events.description: The new five-year strategy focuses on three pillars: Proximity (strengthening local services), Digital Agility (fast pivot to online and social media), and Bringing Canadians Together. The plan aims to expand audiences by reaching Canadians who undervalue or do not use CBC services, including younger demographics and new Canadians.
recent_events.impact: Signals a major strategic shift toward digital-first operations and audience expansion beyond traditional users, aiming to demonstrate public value in an era of funding scrutiny

recent_events.title: Federal Budget 2025 provides $150 million in additional CBC/Radio-Canada funding
recent_events.description: The Liberal government's 2025 budget allocated $150 million to CBC/Radio-Canada to strengthen its mandate and modernize its operations, plus an additional $42 million from the 2024 Fall Economic Statement, bringing total 2025-26 funding to approximately $1.57 billion.
recent_events.impact: Significant reinvestment in public broadcasting, though temporary, with the boost set to expire the following fiscal year

recent_events.title: Federal government plans to reduce CBC funding by approximately $192 million in 2026-27
recent_events.description: The temporary funding boost provided in 2025-26 expires and will not be renewed, reducing CBC's budget from approximately $1.57 billion back to around $1.38 billion for 2026-27. This comes despite earlier Liberal promises to increase permanent annual funding.
recent_events.impact: Significant funding reduction creating renewed financial pressure on the public broadcaster as it attempts to execute its digital transformation strategy

recent_events.title: CBC President Bouchard discusses the future of public broadcasting in Canada
recent_events.description: In a CBC Front Burner podcast interview, Marie-Philippe Bouchard discussed the existential threats facing CBC, the digital transformation strategy, and the importance of public broadcasting for Canadian democracy and culture. She acknowledged the corporation must demonstrate its value to all Canadians.
recent_events.impact: Public articulation of the strategic vision and challenges facing CBC under new leadership

core_business: 加拿大广播公司（CBC/Radio-Canada）是加拿大的国家公共广播机构，成立于1936年11月2日，是加拿大现存历史最悠久的广播网络。作为联邦皇家企业（Crown Corporation），CBC依据1991年《广播法》运营，通过议会拨款获得约12亿至15亿加元的年度公共资金，同时通过电视广告、数字平台订阅等商业收入补充运营。CBC运营两大全国性电视网络（英语CBC Television和法语Ici Radio-Canada Tele）、四个地面广播电台网络（英语CBC Radio One和CBC Music，法语Ici Radio-Canada Premiere和Ici Musique）、多个专业频道（CBC News Network、Ici RDI、Ici Explora、Ici ARTV、Documentary Channel）、数字流媒体平台（CBC Gem、Ici TOU.TV、CBC Listen）以及北部地区特别服务（CBC North/Radio-Canada Nord），并用英语、法语和八种原住民语言进行广播。2023年员工约9,429人，年收入约19亿加元（含公共拨款）。CBC News是加拿大最大的广播新闻采集机构。2025年新任总裁兼CEO Marie-Philippe Bouchard发布了2025-2030年战略计划，重点推进数字化转型和本土服务强化。
apec_stance: 作为加拿大国家公共广播机构，CBC/Radio-Canada在APEC相关事务中扮演信息传播和公共舆论引导的重要角色。CBC News对APEC峰会、亚太地区贸易政策、加太经济关系等进行持续报道和分析，为加拿大公众和决策者提供关于APEC经济体动态的深度信息。CBC与亚太地区公共广播机构（如日本NHK、韩国KBS、澳大利亚ABC等）保持内容合作和新闻交流关系，在促进加拿大与APEC经济体之间的文化理解和信息流通方面发挥作用。在当前加美贸易紧张局势和亚太市场多元化战略背景下，CBC的新闻报道对塑造加拿大公众对APEC区域合作的认知具有重要影响力。2025-2030年战略中的数字化转型也旨在更好地服务包括亚太裔新移民在内的多元文化群体。
